questions.q: Per this lesson, what specific problem does SIWE solve that an arbitrary, unstructured signed message doesn't?
options: An unstructured message is replayable across sites and doesn't guarantee the user knew what they were agreeing to; SIWE standardizes the message so this can be checked safely
Wallets cannot sign arbitrary messages at all without SIWE
SIWE eliminates the need for any cryptographic signature entirely
SIWE allows a server to directly read a user's private key for verification
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that signing itself isn't new — the problem is that a free-text message is replayable and ambiguous, which EIP-4361's structure fixes.

questions.q: What role does the `domain` field play in a SIWE message, per this lesson?
options: It's what lets a wallet detect phishing, by checking that the domain requesting the signature matches where the request actually came from
It specifies which blockchain network the session will run on
It sets how long the session will remain valid after signing
It has no functional role and exists purely for display purposes
questions.explain: The lesson explains EIP-4361 requires wallets to verify the domain matches the actual requester, which is the core anti-phishing mechanism.

questions.q: What does the `nonce` field in a SIWE message specifically prevent, according to this lesson?
options: A captured signature being replayed for a second login, since it's a fresh, server-issued value checked against each attempt
The user from seeing the message before signing it
The message from being longer than 256 characters
The wallet from signing more than one message per session
questions.explain: The lesson defines nonce as the field stopping replay attacks — a captured signature can't be reused because the nonce won't match a new login attempt.

questions.q: In the flow this lesson describes, what happens before the wallet signs the SIWE message?
options: The backend generates and issues a nonce, which the frontend includes when building the message
The backend immediately starts a session with no prior steps
The user must manually type their private key into the frontend
The wallet generates its own message with no input from the frontend or backend
questions.explain: The six-step flow in the lesson starts with the backend issuing a nonce before the frontend builds and signs the message.

questions.q: What does `message.prepareMessage()` do in the real `siwe` library usage shown in this lesson?
options: Turns the structured SiweMessage fields into the exact ABNF-conformant string that gets signed by the wallet
Sends the message directly to the blockchain as a transaction
Verifies the signature against the message on the server
Generates a new private key for the user's wallet
questions.explain: The lesson explains prepareMessage() produces the exact spec-conformant string to sign, which matters because Lesson 22's server-side verification depends on that exact format.
